title: Crispy Tofu and Snap Pea Stir-Fry with Ginger-Garlic Sauce
description: Cornstarch-crusted tofu, snap peas, mushrooms, and bell pepper tossed in a glossy tamari, ginger, and garlic sauce that clings instead of pooling on the plate.
equipment: 12-inch nonstick or carbon-steel skillet or wok
clean kitchen towel for pressing tofu
notes: Press the tofu by wrapping it in a clean towel and setting a heavy pan on top for 15 minutes; drier tofu browns better and spatters less. Tamari is usually gluten-free but check the label, or use regular soy sauce if gluten is not a concern (the dish then contains wheat). Have everything cut and the sauce mixed before you turn on the heat, because the cooking goes quickly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days; the tofu softens but the flavor holds. Cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate it within 1 hour, then reheat until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu, pressed for 15 minutes and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
neutral oil such as avocado or canola, divided
cremini or shiitake mushrooms, stemmed if shiitake, sliced 1/4 inch thick
large red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
scallions, thinly sliced, white and green parts kept separate

instructions: Pat the pressed tofu cubes dry. In a medium bowl, toss them gently with the salt and 2 tablespoons of the cornstarch until every side has a thin, dusty coating.
In a small bowl, whisk the water, tamari, rice vinegar, maple syrup, sesame oil, and the remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch until no lumps remain. Set the sauce next to the stove.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the neutral oil in a 12-inch skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning the cubes every 2 minutes, until golden and crisp on most sides. Transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil to the pan, still over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring once or twice, until they release their liquid and brown at the edges. Add the bell pepper and snap peas and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until bright and crisp-tender.
Push the vegetables to the sides, add the garlic, ginger, and scallion whites to the center, and stir for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant.

Whisk the sauce again (the cornstarch settles), pour it into the pan, and stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes as it comes to a simmer, until it turns glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Return the tofu to the pan and toss for 30 seconds to coat. Scatter the scallion greens over the top and serve right away over the rice.

title: Smoky Black Bean Burgers That Hold Together
description: Oven-dried black beans, panko, and one egg make a firm patty with a crisp crust and a tender middle, seasoned with cumin and smoked paprika. They flip cleanly in a skillet.
notes: Drying the beans in the oven is what keeps these from turning mushy, so do not skip it. Leave about a third of the beans whole for texture. Shaped raw patties can be covered and refrigerated for up to 24 hours, which firms them further. Because the mixture contains raw egg, cook the patties until the center reaches 160°F. Refrigerate cooked patties within 2 hours and keep for up to 4 days, or freeze them between sheets of parchment for up to 3 months; reheat from frozen in a 375°F oven for 15 to 18 minutes. These are too delicate for open grill grates; use a griddle or a skillet set on the grill. Many burger buns contain milk or egg, so check the label if that matters to you.

ingredients.name: black beans (15 oz each), drained, rinsed, and patted dry
small yellow onion, finely diced (about 3/4 cup)

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Spread the drained beans in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes, until the skins split and the beans feel dry to the touch. Let them cool for 5 minutes.

While the beans bake, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and lightly golden.

Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, and tomato paste to the onion and stir for 1 minute, until the paste darkens and the spices smell toasty. Scrape the mixture into a large bowl and wipe out the skillet.

Add the beans to the bowl and mash with a potato masher or fork until about two-thirds are broken down and the rest are still whole or halved. Stir in the egg, panko, pepper, and remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt until evenly combined. Let the mixture rest for 10 minutes so the panko absorbs moisture; a handful should hold its shape when squeezed.
Divide the mixture into 6 portions of about 1/2 cup each. Press each one firmly into a patty about 3 1/2 inches wide and 3/4 inch thick, smoothing any cracks around the edge.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in the skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Cook 3 patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side, flipping once with a thin spatula, until a deep brown crust forms and the center reaches 160°F. Repeat with the remaining oil and patties.
Serve the burgers on the toasted buns with tomato, lettuce, and any sauces you like.

title: Horiatiki-Style Salad with Lemony Butter Beans
description: A lettuce-free Greek village salad of tomatoes, cucumber, green pepper, olives, and slabs of feta, made into a full lunch with butter beans marinated in oregano, lemon, and olive oil.
notes: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find and block feta packed in brine, which is creamier and less salty-sharp than pre-crumbled. Some feta is made with animal rennet; look for one labeled vegetarian or made with microbial rennet if that matters to you. The beans can marinate in the dressing, covered and refrigerated, for up to 3 days and only get better. Once the tomatoes and cucumber are added, the salad is at its best within 2 hours and keeps refrigerated for 1 day, though the vegetables soften and release juice. Do not leave it at room temperature for more than 2 hours. Cannellini beans work in place of butter beans.

ingredients.name: butter beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
ripe tomatoes, cored and cut into 1-inch wedges or chunks
English cucumber, halved lengthwise and sliced 1/2 inch thick
green bell pepper, seeded and sliced into thin rings
block feta in brine, drained and cut into 4 thick slabs

instructions: In a large serving bowl, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, 1 teaspoon of the oregano, 1/2 teaspoon of the salt, and the pepper until the dressing looks cloudy and blended.
Add the butter beans and red onion to the bowl and fold gently to coat. Let them marinate at room temperature for 15 minutes, which seasons the beans and takes the raw edge off the onion.
While the beans marinate, put the tomatoes in a separate bowl, sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, and let them sit for about 10 minutes so they start to release their juices.
Add the tomatoes and their juices, the cucumber, bell pepper, and olives to the beans. Toss gently with a large spoon, lifting from the bottom so the beans stay whole.
Lay the feta slabs on top, sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon oregano, and spoon a little dressing from the bottom of the bowl over the cheese. Serve at once, breaking up the feta at the table.

title: Kale and Quinoa Caesar with Crispy Chickpeas
description: Massaged lacinato kale and fluffy quinoa in a creamy tahini, caper, and lemon dressing with the briny, garlicky punch of a Caesar, topped with oven-crisped chickpeas instead of croutons.
notes: Capers and their brine stand in for the anchovy, and nutritional yeast adds the savory note Parmesan would. Dry the chickpeas thoroughly with a towel; wet chickpeas steam instead of crisping. Check the labels on Dijon mustard and nutritional yeast if you need the salad strictly gluten-free. Cool the quinoa quickly and refrigerate it within 1 hour if you are not using it right away. Dressed kale is sturdy and keeps refrigerated for up to 2 days; the dressing alone keeps 5 days and thickens when cold, so loosen it with a teaspoon of water. Store the chickpeas separately, loosely covered at room temperature, and add them just before eating, since they soften within a day.

ingredients.name: quinoa, rinsed well in a fine-mesh strainer
chickpeas (15 oz), drained, rinsed, and patted very dry
capers, drained and finely chopped, plus 1 tablespoon of their brine
cold water, plus more as needed
lacinato kale (about 1 lb total), stems removed, leaves sliced into thin ribbons

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Combine the quinoa, 1 1/2 cups water, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt in a small saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains show small white rings. Rest covered for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork, and spread on a plate to cool.

While the quinoa cooks, toss the chickpeas on a rimmed baking sheet with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, the garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Roast for 22 to 28 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until deep golden and crisp enough to rattle on the pan.

For the dressing, whisk the tahini, lemon juice, chopped capers and brine, nutritional yeast, mustard, garlic, pepper, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, and remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in a bowl. It will seize and thicken at first. Whisk in the 3 tablespoons cold water, then more by the teaspoon, until smooth and thick but pourable.

Put the kale in a large bowl and pour over half of the dressing. Massage with clean hands for 1 to 2 minutes, squeezing the leaves, until they darken, turn tender, and shrink in volume by about a third.
Add the cooled quinoa and most of the remaining dressing and toss until evenly coated. Taste and add the rest of the dressing or a squeeze of lemon if it needs it.
Divide among bowls and top with the crispy chickpeas and the pepitas just before serving so they stay crunchy.

title: Smoky Three-Bean Chili
description: Black, kidney, and pinto beans simmered with crushed tomatoes, bell pepper, and a toasted chili-cumin base until thick and spoon-coating. A squeeze of lime at the end keeps it bright.
equipment: 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven or heavy pot
notes: Chili powder here means the mild American blend, not pure ground chiles; blends and broths occasionally contain gluten, so check labels if needed. For more heat, add a minced jalapeño with the onion or 1/4 teaspoon cayenne with the spices. The chili thickens as it sits and tastes better the next day. Cool it in shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours; it keeps 5 days refrigerated or 3 months frozen. Reheat to a full simmer (165°F), adding a splash of water to loosen. Good toppings: diced avocado, sliced scallions, cilantro, crushed corn tortilla chips, or pickled red onion.

ingredients.name: large red bell pepper, seeded and diced
kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
black beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
red kidney beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
pinto beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and cook for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is translucent and just starting to brown at the edges.

Add the garlic, tomato paste, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the paste darkens to brick red and the spices smell toasty; lower the heat if they start to stick.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and broth and scrape up anything stuck to the bottom of the pot. Stir in all three beans and the remaining 1 teaspoon salt, then bring to a boil over medium-high heat.

Reduce the heat to medium-low, partially cover, and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the chili is thick enough that a spoon dragged across the bottom leaves a trail for a moment. For a thicker body, mash some of the beans against the side of the pot.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the lime juice. Taste and add more salt if needed, let the chili rest for 5 minutes, then ladle into bowls and add toppings.

title: Smoky Roasted Cauliflower Tacos with Lime-Cabbage Slaw
description: Cauliflower roasted hot with chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika until charred at the edges, piled into warm corn tortillas with a crunchy lime and cilantro cabbage slaw and avocado.
notes: Cut the florets to about 1 inch and give them room on the pan; crowded cauliflower steams and will not char. Choose tortillas made from 100 percent corn if you need the tacos gluten-free, since some brands blend in wheat. The slaw can be made up to 4 hours ahead and keeps refrigerated for 2 days, though it softens and turns the juices pink. Refrigerate leftover cauliflower within 2 hours and use within 4 days; reheat on a sheet pan at 425°F for 6 to 8 minutes to bring back the edges. Slice the avocado just before serving so it does not brown.

ingredients.name: large head cauliflower (about 2 lb), cut into 1-inch florets
finely shredded red cabbage (about 1/4 of a small head)

instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the lower third. On a rimmed baking sheet, toss the cauliflower with 3 tablespoons of the olive oil, the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and 3/4 teaspoon of the salt until evenly coated. Spread in a single layer with the cut sides down.
Roast for 22 to 25 minutes, flipping the florets once halfway through, until they are tender when pierced with a knife and deeply browned at the edges.

While the cauliflower roasts, make the slaw. In a medium bowl, toss the cabbage and cilantro with the lime juice, maple syrup, remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Let it sit for at least 10 minutes, until the cabbage softens slightly and tastes bright.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for 30 to 45 seconds per side, until pliable with a few toasted spots. Stack them in a clean towel to keep warm and flexible.
Fill each tortilla with roasted cauliflower, a small pile of slaw, and a slice or two of avocado. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing over the top.

title: Palak Paneer (Spiced Spinach with Paneer)
description: Seared paneer in a smooth, bright green spinach sauce built on cumin, ginger, garlic, and tomato, finished with a little cream and garam masala. Serve with rice or flatbread.
notes: As written, with paneer and cream, this is vegetarian but not vegan. For a vegan version, swap the paneer for 14 oz extra-firm tofu (pressed, cubed, and seared the same way) and use full-fat coconut milk in place of the cream; that version contains soy and no milk. Blanching the spinach briefly and keeping the final simmer short are what hold the green color; long cooking turns it olive drab. A 16-oz bag of frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed, can replace the fresh, and you can skip the blanching. Serve with basmati rice to keep the meal gluten-free, since naan and roti contain wheat. Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days; reheat gently with a splash of water. Cool any leftover rice quickly and refrigerate it within 1 hour.

ingredients.name: neutral oil such as avocado or sunflower, divided
serrano or green chile, finely chopped (seeded for less heat)
kosher salt, plus more to taste

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil over high heat. Add the spinach, push it under, and blanch for 1 minute, just until wilted and bright green. Drain, rinse under cold running water until cool, and squeeze gently to remove most of the water.
Blend the spinach with the 1/2 cup water until smooth, scraping down the blender as needed. Set the puree aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the paneer in a single layer and sear for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once or twice, until golden on two or three sides. Transfer to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 30 seconds, until a shade darker and fragrant. Add the onion and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.

Stir in the garlic, ginger, and chile and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric, and salt and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, mashing with the spoon, until the tomatoes collapse into a thick paste and the oil glistens at the edges.
Pour in the spinach puree and stir well. Simmer over medium-low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the sauce is hot and thick enough to mound on a spoon; add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the cream and garam masala, then fold in the paneer and warm it through for 2 minutes. Take the pan off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, taste for salt, and serve.

title: Fajita Vegetable Burrito Bowls with Cilantro-Lime Rice
description: Skillet-charred peppers and onions with cumin and oregano over cilantro-lime rice and saucy pinto beans, finished with avocado and salsa. Everything keeps well for packed lunches.
notes: For good char, get the skillet very hot and resist stirring more than every couple of minutes. Rinsing the rice until the water runs mostly clear keeps the grains separate. Check the labels on chili powder and salsa if you need the bowls strictly gluten-free. For meal prep, pack rice, beans, and vegetables together and keep the avocado, salsa, and lettuce separate. Cool the rice quickly and refrigerate it within 1 hour; refrigerate everything else within 2 hours. The components keep 4 days refrigerated; reheat the rice, beans, and vegetables until steaming hot, then add the cold toppings.

ingredients.name: long-grain white rice, rinsed until the water runs mostly clear
neutral oil such as avocado or canola
bell peppers in mixed colors, seeded and sliced 1/4 inch thick
large red onion, halved and sliced 1/4 inch thick
pinto beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
large ripe avocado, pitted and diced
tomato salsa or pico de gallo

instructions: Combine the rinsed rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Take the pan off the heat and let it stand, covered, for 10 minutes.

While the rice cooks, heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers and just begins to smoke. Add the peppers and onion in an even layer and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring only every 2 minutes, until charred in spots and crisp-tender.

Sprinkle the chili powder, cumin, oregano, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute, until the spices smell toasty. Add 1 tablespoon of the lime juice, scrape up any browned bits, and transfer the vegetables to a plate.

Return the skillet to medium heat and add the pinto beans, 1/3 cup water, and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, mashing a few beans with the back of a spoon, until the beans are hot and lightly saucy.
Fluff the rice with a fork and fold in the cilantro and the remaining 2 tablespoons lime juice.
Divide the rice among 4 bowls and top with the beans, fajita vegetables, avocado, salsa, and lettuce if using. Serve with extra lime if you like.

title: Caprese Panzanella with Toasted Ciabatta
description: Salted ripe tomatoes, torn fresh mozzarella, and basil tossed with olive oil-toasted ciabatta that soaks up a dressing made from the tomatoes' own juices and red wine vinegar.
equipment: colander set over a large bowl
notes: This salad depends on ripe, in-season tomatoes; a mix of colors and sizes looks and tastes best. Day-old bread is ideal, and the bread can be toasted up to a day ahead and kept in an airtight container at room temperature. Plan on a 15- to 20-minute rest after tossing, then serve; panzanella is at its best within 2 hours of dressing, while the bread still has some chew. Leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 1 day, but the bread turns soft. Because of the fresh mozzarella, do not leave the salad at room temperature for more than 2 hours. Some mozzarella is made with animal rennet, so check the label if you need it strictly vegetarian.

ingredients.name: ripe mixed tomatoes, cored and cut into bite-size chunks (cherry tomatoes halved)
ciabatta or rustic country bread, torn into 1-inch pieces (about 6 cups)
fresh mozzarella, torn into bite-size pieces
loosely packed fresh basil leaves, torn

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Put the tomatoes in a colander set over a large bowl, toss with 1 teaspoon of the salt, and let them drain for 15 minutes, tossing once or twice. You should collect at least 1/4 cup of juice in the bowl.

Meanwhile, toss the torn bread on a rimmed baking sheet with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring once, until golden and crisp on the outside but still slightly chewy in the center. Let it cool on the pan.

Lift the colander of tomatoes off the bowl and set it aside. Add the shallot, garlic, vinegar, and pepper to the tomato juices, then whisk in the remaining 4 tablespoons olive oil in a slow stream until the dressing looks blended.

Add the toasted bread and the drained tomatoes to the bowl and toss well. Let the salad rest for 15 to 20 minutes, tossing once or twice, until the bread has absorbed most of the dressing but the edges still have some crunch.
Fold in the mozzarella and basil. Taste, add a pinch more salt or a splash of vinegar if needed, and serve at room temperature.

title: Sweet Potato and Lentil Nourish Bowls with Sunflower-Ginger Dressing
description: Brown rice, tender green lentils, and cumin-roasted sweet potato and broccoli with fresh spinach and radishes, tied together by a creamy lime and ginger dressing made from sunflower seed butter.
notes: The dressing uses sunflower seed butter instead of peanut or tree nut butter; if you are cooking for someone with a nut allergy, choose seed butter and pepitas from a nut-free facility. Unsweetened seed butter works best; if yours is sweetened, leave out the maple syrup and add it to taste. Start the rice first, since it takes the longest. Cool the rice and lentils quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; refrigerate the roasted vegetables within 2 hours. Stored separately, the components keep 4 days and the dressing 5 days (thin it with a teaspoon of water after chilling). Assemble and dress the bowls just before eating; a dressed bowl holds for a few hours in a lunch box with an ice pack, but the spinach wilts.

ingredients.name: green or brown lentils, picked over and rinsed
medium sweet potatoes (about 1 1/4 lb), scrubbed and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
broccoli (1 medium head), cut into bite-size florets
warm water, plus more as needed

instructions: Combine the rice, 2 cups water, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 40 to 45 minutes, until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed. Let it stand, covered, off the heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F. On a rimmed baking sheet, toss the sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, the cumin, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Spread them out and roast for 15 minutes.

While the sweet potatoes roast, put the lentils in a second saucepan with 3 cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape. Drain well and toss with 1/4 teaspoon of the salt.

Toss the broccoli with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Add it to the baking sheet, stir everything together, and roast for 15 to 18 minutes more, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized underneath and the broccoli is browned at the tips.

For the dressing, whisk the sunflower seed butter, lime juice, maple syrup, ginger, garlic, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in a small bowl; it will look stiff at first. Whisk in the warm water a tablespoon at a time until the dressing is smooth and drizzles easily from a spoon.
Divide the rice among 4 bowls and arrange the lentils, roasted vegetables, spinach, and radishes on top. Drizzle generously with the dressing and sprinkle with the pepitas.
